technical_body.channels: 30 kHz FM, 832 channels per operator across the A/B (non-wireline/wireline) bands

control_channel.focc: Forward Control Channel — CO to handset, 10 kbps Manchester-encoded data
control_channel.recc: Reverse Control Channel — handset to CO, 10 kbps Manchester

identity.min: Mobile ID Number — 34 bits, derived from the 10-digit MDN
identity.esn: Electronic Serial Number — 32 bits, 8-bit manufacturer + 24-bit serial. Programmed at manufacture; supposed to be immutable.

technical_body.cleartext_leak: On registration, the handset sends MIN + ESN in the clear over the RECC. Anyone with a scanner and decoder could capture and clone.
technical_body.defenses_added: IS-54B / IS-136 (TDMA) and PCS operators added the 'A-Key' authentication starting 1996-1998, which effectively killed pure clone fraud on properly-provisioned lines.
technical_body.shutoff: FCC-authorized AMPS sunset Feb 18, 2008 in the US. Analog was largely obsolete in urban markets by 2003.

identity.imsi: International Mobile Subscriber Identity — stored on the SIM
identity.ki: 128-bit secret key on the SIM; never transmitted
identity.imei: International Mobile Equipment Identity — the phone hardware ID

authentication.a3_a8: Operator-defined; most used COMP128-1, broken by Wagner/Goldberg/Briceno 1998. A physical clone required ~150k challenges but was tractable. COMP128-2 and COMP128-3 followed.
authentication.a5_1: Western Europe and US encryption. Practical rainbow-table attack landed 2008-2010 (Karsten Nohl). PRE-2004 A5/1 was still considered 'hard' outside academia.
authentication.a5_2: Weakened export version. Ciphertext-only attack by Barkan/Biham/Keller in 2003.
authentication.a5_0: Encryption off — used in some jurisdictions for lawful intercept simplification.

disputed.a5_1_break_date: The corpus MUST NOT claim A5/1 was practically broken by 2003. Biryukov/Shamir/Wagner 2000 needed precomputation few had done in the wild. Practical break arrived 2008-2010.

technical_body.overlay_on: AMPS — used unused voice channels (CDPD 'channel hopping' avoided interference with active voice calls)
technical_body.encryption: RC4 with a session key derived from a shared secret
technical_body.notable_attacks: MDBS (Mobile Data Base Station) spoofing was documented; the shared-secret handshake was replayable in some deployments.
technical_body.used_for: PocketNet, early wireless credit-card readers, dispatch data terminals, first-gen wireless PDAs (Palm VII on OmniSky).

technical_body.encryption: None — cap codes and message bodies broadcast in the clear.
eavesdrop_stack: ICOM PCR-1000 or Radio Shack Pro-2006 scanner
PDW or POC32 PC-based decoder software
Tens of thousands of messages/day passively logged from one metro
sensitive_traffic: On-call SRE / NOC alerts (server hostnames, sometimes credentials)
White House Communications Agency (WHCA) traffic — WikiLeaks published 9/11-era WHCA pages in 2009

name: POCSAG (Post Office Code Standardization Advisory Group)

technical_body.band: 925-940 MHz commercial paging in North America
technical_body.notable: The older, slower predecessor to FLEX. Coexisted through the late 1990s; many low-end alphanumeric pagers stayed on POCSAG.

exposes: field-service menu (RSSI, cell ID, active channel)
technical_body.notes: The '837866' digits spell 'TEST-MOTO' on a phone keypad.

technical_body.handset_family: Motorola 2000-XL and related transportable bag phones
OKI 900 and OKI 1150 (Tandy/Radio Shack rebadges: CT-300/CT-500)
technical_body.notable: The most-hackable AMPS phone of its generation. Firmware was extractable; community loaders 'Roger-Wilco' and 'N0kIA loader' let you flash custom firmware that logged every MIN/ESN pair broadcast on the RECC in listening range.
technical_body.phreak_relevance: OKI 900s became the de-facto AMPS scanner platform of the mid-90s. A modded OKI 900 in a car could clone every phone that registered in a given cell overnight.

technical_body.notes: The joystick-based entry sequence is why third-hand tutorials often transcribed this wrong.

technical_body.entry_sequence: Fcn 0, then 111111 at the NAM prompt
